citing_sentences: In electric power systems and wholesale electricity markets, the operational value of wind power forecasting is governed by asymmetric decision losses in unit commitment, economic dispatch, and real-time balancing settlement \cite{holttinen2021,weron2014}.
However, power system operations demonstrate that statistical error reductions do not guarantee economic value under asymmetric market penalties \cite{weron2014,zhang2014wind}.

In operational power system balancing, transmission system operators evaluate declared bids under asymmetric pinball dispatch penalties \cite{weron2014,zhang2014wind}: \begin{equation} \ell(p, Y; r) = c_+ \max(p - Y, 0) + c_- \max(Y - p, 0), \label{eq:pinball_loss} \end{equation} where $p \in [0, 1]$ is the declared dispatch commitment, $c_+$ is the shortfall unit penalty (under-generation where declared power exceeds physical delivery, $p > Y$, requiring expensive tertiary reserve activation), $c_-$ is the surplus unit penalty (over-generation, $Y > p$, inducing downward redispatch or curtailment), and $r = c_+ / c_-$ represents the cost asymmetry ratio.
